Pulmonary Fibrosis 
Like scars that develop on the skin, pulmonary fibrosis involves scarring of the lung tissue (Krishna et al., 2022). 
Scar or fibrotic tissue does not function normally in gas exchange. The fibrotic tissue prevents oxygen flow from the 
alveoli into the bloodstream, leading to low oxygen levels and compromised lung capacity as the scar tissue stiffens. 
Pulmonary fibrosis etiology might be idiopathic or secondary to another illness, medication, radiation therapy, or 
environmental exposure (Agarwal & Huda, 2022; Krishna et al., 2022). 
Nutritional intake significantly impacts clinical outcomes for individuals with pulmonary fibrosis. Nutrients are in 
high demand due to the increase in respiratory workload, activation of inflammatory mediators, hypoxemia, and lack 
of physical exercise (Faverio et al., 2020). As with COPD, malnutrition remains prevalent for those with inadequate 
nutrition intake. Some preferred treatment medications for pulmonary fibrosis cause diarrhea and other adverse
